Add guidance for testing, rollback, monitoring, and approval before adding cron or systemd schedules.
Advise users to scope root filesystem scans and avoid running them on sensitive hosts without approval.

content.value_statement: System administrators need repeatable steps for shell failures and host issues. This skill organizes diagnostics, script quality checks, testing, and automation planning.
actual_capabilities: Guides OS environment assessment with version, resource, process, and network checks.
Organizes shell script linting with ShellCheck and structured review steps.
Provides debugging patterns using shell options, logging, traps, and syntax checks.
Supplies a defensive Bash script template with argument handling and help output.
Outlines Bats test cases for success, error, and file output behavior.
Summarizes troubleshooting commands for logs, services, disk, memory, and connectivity.
limitations: It does not execute commands, install tools, or inspect the host by itself.
Examples may need adaptation for specific Linux, macOS, or Windows environments.
Privileged commands and scheduled jobs require human review before use.
It does not replace organization change control or security approval processes.

use_cases.title: Fix Script Failures
use_cases.description: Review a failing shell script with linting, debug tracing, and focused checks before changing production behavior.

use_cases.title: Triage Host Incidents
use_cases.description: Follow a structured path for logs, resources, connectivity, and service state during an operating system issue.

use_cases.title: Plan Maintenance Automation
use_cases.description: Design scripts, tests, scheduling, and monitoring for recurring system administration tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Simple Script Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this OS scripting workflow to inspect my shell script failure. Focus on environment checks, ShellCheck findings, and safe debugging steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Safer Bash Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the script development phase to design a Bash script for backups. Include validation, logging, help text, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing phase to outline Bats tests for my shell automation. Cover success, missing input, and expected output cases.

prompt_templates.title: Triage a Production Host Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the full workflow to diagnose high resource usage on a Linux host. Prioritize read-only checks, logs, process analysis, and rollback-safe actions.

output_examples.input: A shell script fails only on one Linux server.
output_examples.output: A phased investigation plan covering environment details, lint findings, debug tracing, logs, and isolated reproduction steps.

output_examples.input: A team wants a daily backup automation workflow.
output_examples.output: A practical checklist for script structure, input validation, logging, tests, scheduling review, and operational monitoring.

output_examples.input: A service outage may be caused by resource pressure.
output_examples.output: A read-only triage sequence for process load, memory pressure, disk usage, network state, service logs, and next actions.

best_practices: Start with read-only diagnostics before changing packages, services, or scheduled tasks.
Run ShellCheck and tests before using generated scripts in production.
Review privileged commands and cron changes with a human operator.
anti_patterns: Do not copy shell examples into production without checking paths, permissions, and data impact.
Do not run broad filesystem searches on sensitive hosts without scope limits.
Do not add scheduled automation before logging, monitoring, and rollback are planned.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and example commands that require user review before execution.

faq.question: Which operating systems does it support?
faq.answer: It covers Linux, macOS, and Windows workflows, with many examples focused on Unix shell environments.

faq.question: Can it help create new scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides script structure, argument parsing, logging, validation, help text, and error handling.

faq.question: Is it safe for production systems?
faq.answer: Use it with change control. Review privileged commands, filesystem scans, and scheduled tasks before applying changes.

faq.question: Does it replace ShellCheck?
faq.answer: No. It points users toward ShellCheck and adds surrounding review, debugging, and testing workflow steps.

faq.question: How does it help during incidents?
faq.answer: It organizes host triage around symptoms, logs, resources, connectivity, service state, and careful fix validation.
